```{python}
#| label: hero-image
#| output: false

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from plotnine import *

# Honeycomb grid: 5 rows × 10 cols of hexagons
centers = []
for row in range(5):
    for col in range(10):
        x = col * np.sqrt(3)
        y = -row * 1.5
        if row % 2 == 1:
            x += np.sqrt(3) / 2
        centers.append((x, y))

angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 7)
hex_data = pd.concat(
    [
        pd.DataFrame({
            "x": cx + np.cos(angles),
            "y": cy + np.sin(angles),
            "group": i,
        })
        for i, (cx, cy) in enumerate(centers)
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
)

(
    ggplot(hex_data, aes(x="x", y="y", group="group"))
    + geom_polygon(fill="#dcdcdc", color="white", size=2)
    + coord_equal()
    + theme_void()
    + theme(
        figure_size=(8, 3.5),
        plot_background=element_rect(fill="white", color="white"),
    )
).save("hero-image.png", dpi=150, verbose=False)
```

![](hero-image.png)

Extending plotnine is a powerful way to enhance productivity and make creating plots more fun. The plotnine extension system allows us to build new 'vocabulary' for more fluent expression.

<!-- Yet some useful areas of extension are not in mainstream use even among seasoned ggplot2 users. -->

'Easy geom_\*() recipes' is a new point of entry for learning plotnine *Stat* extension, a particularly exension powerful mechanism which allows users to define computation to be used in new geom\_\*() or stat\_\*() functions.

With new Stats, *you* can specify calculation to be done within the plotnine plot pipeline:

```{python}
#| eval: false
(
    ggplot(data=cars, aes(x="speed", y="dist"))
    + geom_customized()  # YOU specify compute
)
```

In this project's tutorials, you'll see how to define your own Stats and write new user-facing geom\_\*() or stat\_\*() functions.

The materials are aimed at academics, data analysts, BI professionals, seasoned and new plotnine users, statistics educators and their students, journalists, etc. The approach has been tested and evaluated by data science and statistics educators.
